Aria Johnson: Following the postmortem, we need a concise follow-up thread to lock owners and timelines for runbook/playbook changes. Key gaps: missing explicit triage commands, unclear escalation sequence, no guarded-branch QA flow.
Marcus Lee: Agreed. I'll take triage commands and runnable snippets. Aim to include exact curl/kubectl/rbctl lines so oncall can copy/paste. Due 2026-04-12.
Fiona Zhang: I'll draft the escalation sequence and the owner rotation table. Also add sample pager messages. Due 2026-04-10.
Aria Johnson: For recurrence tracking, attach links to the related incidents and add a short "pattern summary" in the runbook intro. Marcus, include a line linking incidents 2419009999 and 2421234567.
Marcus Lee: Example triage commands to add to the runbook:
```
# eviction rate
curl -sS http://metrics.internal/kvcache?model=slot | jq .evictions_per_min
# prefix size
curl -sS http://metrics.internal/kvcache?model=slot | jq .prefix_size_mb
# quick canary probe
curl -sS http://canary.inference/v1/health | jq .status
# dry-run route swap
rbctl route swap --model slot --from canary --to stable --dry-run
# isolate shard
rbctl shards set --model slot --shard SHARD_ID --state isolate
# revert rollout
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/serving-main
```
Fiona Zhang: Nice. Thresholds to codify next to the commands: evictions_per_min >= 80 -> begin triage; >=180 -> escalate runtime lead; prefix_size_mb > 500 -> consider shard isolation. Canary health != "ok" -> do not promote.
Aria Johnson: For escalation, propose exact paging order with copy/paste message: oncall -> runtime lead -> infra oncall -> eng manager. Include pager IDs and a one-line summary template.
